causal_chain: Full-sort ranking should improve most on sparse or multi-interest users, lifting NDCG@10.
Infer a per-user support subset of historical interactions for each positive target.
This suppresses brittle co-occurrence shortcuts and distributes user evidence across the truly explanatory history.
Train pairwise scores to stay stable when non-support interactions are counterfactually removed.
blind_projection.closest_parent: A recommender that learns which historical interactions most support each positive target and explicitly trains ranking margins to remain stable when those support interactions are removed will generalize better in offline top-n recommendation than a matched model trained only on factual pairwise ranking, because it suppresses brittle shortcut co-occurrence reliance and promotes support-distributed user representations.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: The gain comes from generic regularization or popularity suppression, not from isolatable support transport.
discriminative_predictions: A matched regularized BPR control should not reproduce the same sparse-user uplift if the support-router is the real cause.
If generic regularization is the true explanation, a popularity/L2-matched control should close most of the gap without learning support weights.
When support interactions are removed at evaluation, the proposed model should degrade less than the control.
expected_evidence: Higher full-sort NDCG@10 than the matched BPR control on the frozen ML-1M split.
Largest improvement concentrated in users with short histories or mixed tastes.
Learned support weights should be non-uniform and align with historically explanatory items.
Lower score sensitivity under support-interaction deletion than the control.
blind_projection.falsifier: No NDCG@10 gain over the matched control, no sparse-user advantage, and no reduction in sensitivity to support removal.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This is not a low-change wrapper: it adds a new support-routing interaction structure plus a counterfactual stability objective and an explicit mechanism-off path, changing both training procedure and executable capability.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A support-routed pairwise recommender with counterfactual support deletion will improve full-sort NDCG@10 by learning which past interactions truly justify each positive item and by rejecting brittle co-occurrence shortcuts.
implementation_requirements: per-user support scorer over historical interactions
same frozen split and negative-sampling protocol
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Keep encoder family, optimizer, batch budget, and evaluation code fixed; only remove the support router and counterfactual deletion loss in the control.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Add a learned support router over user history and a counterfactual stability loss that penalizes ranking changes when non-support interactions are masked.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Replace the support router with uniform history aggregation and set the counterfactual deletion loss weight to zero, reducing to the matched plain pairwise baseline.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: Train the proposed model and its off-switch control on the frozen ML-1M split, then compare full-sort NDCG@10 overall and on the shortest-history user bucket; the wedge is positive only if the model improves both aggregate ranking and sparse-user robustness.
blind_projection.research_question: Can a pairwise collaborative filter that routes each user through a learned support subset of their history and is trained to remain stable under support deletion improve frozen-ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10, especially for sparse users, over a matched BPR baseline?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: The support router and deletion loss add modest overhead but should fit within the 10 GPU-minute qualification budget on the frozen ML-1M protocol.
